UNH.rationale: UNH presents a mixed but mildly attractive picture. On the positive side, the company is a dominant healthcare franchise with 30% Medicare Advantage market share, strong cash generation ($8.9B operating cash flow in Q1 2026), and a dual-engine model combining insurance and health services. Revenue grew modestly YoY (+2.0% in Q1 2026) and the medical care ratio has been improving. However, several significant headwinds temper enthusiasm: (1) The stock has already rallied ~80% from its 2025 low of $234.60 to $431.68, and the P/E has expanded from ~10-12x in mid-2025 to 30.7x currently—near the top of its 365-day range (9.5-30.7). This is expensive vs. its own recent history. (2) Net margin has compressed from 5.6% in July 2025 to 2.8% currently, and ROE has fallen from 22.8% to 12.3%, indicating fundamental deterioration. (3) Ongoing DOJ investigations into Medicare billing, FTC settlement on insulin pricing, and claims denial lawsuits create regulatory overhang. (4) The company had to reduce Medicare Advantage membership by ~1.3 million lives to protect margins, signaling structural challenges. The upcoming Q2 earnings on July 16 (with options implying 6.1% move) could serve as a near-term catalyst, with Bernstein expecting EPS of $5.22 vs. consensus $4.84, but this is already partially priced in given the stock's strong run. The score reflects a quality franchise at a stretched valuation with meaningful regulatory and operational risks.
